text:
mira: Quick smoke request from NewtWorks — they merged nw-lora-v1 and after applying our int4 profile some invoice lines show missing cents or swapped separators. Can someone run a short compat + int4 smoke against hosted int4? they sent a 32-example mini-pack.

kevin: taking this. can you paste a few of the problematic lines?

mira: sure, their QA flagged these three examples: 
- Invoice total: $12,345.67
- Factura total: 12.345,67 

- Charge: A12345,67
They say some renders become "12345" or "12300" after merge+int4.

oscar: queued job on shadow-runner (rdx-medium) with quant=int4 + adapter=nw-lora-v1. id eva-1791234567-a. ETA ~6m.

eval-bot: queued eva-1791234567-a on runner-4. est runtime 5m.

oscar: command used:
```
redwood eval run --model rdx-medium-3b --adapter nw-lora-v1 --quant int4 --tasks currency-format,numeric-precision --samples 32 --out /tmp/newt-smoke.json
```

oscar: quick summary: PPL(base)=10.1, PPL(merged)=11.0 (+8.9%). Numeric mismatches: 5/32 (cents missing/rounded), token-boundary diffs: 4/32. One example where "12,345.67" tokenized as ["12", ",", "345", ".", "67"] -> merged output dropped ".67" token.

kevin: any idea if NewtWorks used a different tokenizer or preprocessing?

mira: they mentioned using a custom normalization that strips non-digit chars and a locale tag token during finetune. SE ticket attached but not the exact recipe yet.

oscar: ran additional runs: (1) same eval with tokenizer_v2 flag -> PPL(merged,tokenizer_v2)=10.6 (delta +4.9%), token diffs reduced to 1/32 (only one euro case left). (2) int8 eval: PPL(merged,int8)=10.3 (delta +2.0%), numeric mismatches down to 2/32. So quant=int4 amplifies existing issues.

kevin: inspected adapter delta norms; layer 5 rows have a few values >1.4. I tried a clamp-merge (clip deltas to [-0.6,0.6]) and re-ran int4 smoke locally: mismatches reduced to 0/32, PPL penalty ~+1.6% vs base. Script I used: 
```
python tools/merge_adapter.py --adapter nw-lora-v1 --clip 0.6 --out merged-nw-clamped.safetensors
```
Pushed a temp gist: https://gist.github.com/temp/nw-clamp-2026

mira: good. Another orthogonal test: a pre-tokenize separator remap (map '.'->',' for euros and normalize thousands) removed most boundary diffs but did not fix rounding where cents disappeared. so two distinct vectors: tokenizer mismatch vs adapter rounding bias.

oscar: I also pulled logits for the failing example; after int4 the softmax mass shifts slightly towards the integer token, likely because quant noise changes relative logits. Not extreme but enough to drop low-prob cents token.

sean: action items: 1) ask NewtWorks for their tokenizer recipe + any normalization/locale tag used during training; 2) recommend retraining with mixed decimal formats and without aggressive rounding augment; 3) add the 32 examples to onboarding-regress/newtworks.json labeled "currency-cents-loss"; 4) offer clamp-merge as temporary mitigation and tokenizer_v2/remap guidance.

kevin: I'll open a short onboarding ticket and attach eval artifacts + the clamp gist. Also will request full training seeds from SE.

mira: please cc @support-ops and @product for visibility.

oscar: marking smoke as "investigate -> pending-customer" for now.

mira: thanks everyone :pray:
